gpu-screen-recorder on Omarchy

Shadowplay-style, GPU-accelerated screen recording for Linux.

To install gpu-screen-recorder on Omarchy, open a terminal and run omarchy pkg add gpu-screen-recorder. It is a 211.4 KB download (452.5 KB installed), version 5.12.3-2, licensed GPL-3.0-only. A shadowplay-like screen recorder for Linux. The fastest screen recorder for Linux. Free and open source.

Install gpu-screen-recorder on Omarchy

gpu-screen-recorder is a lightweight, high-performance screen recorder for Linux that offloads capture and encoding to the GPU, minimizing the performance hit compared to typical CPU-based recorders. It works on both X11 and Wayland across AMD, Intel, and NVIDIA GPUs (plus Apple Silicon via Asahi Linux with software encoding), and supports plain recording, live streaming, instant-replay clips, and screenshots. This package is the core command-line tool; a separate GTK-based GUI exists as its own project.

  1. Open a terminal.
  2. Run the install command:
    omarchy pkg add gpu-screen-recorder
  3. Check it landed. Pacman should list version 5.12.3-2:
    pacman -Qi gpu-screen-recorder

Open and use gpu-screen-recorder

gpu-screen-recorder has no window of its own: it is a command-line tool, library or system component. To see the commands it added to your PATH:

pacman -Ql gpu-screen-recorder | grep /usr/bin/

gpu-screen-recorder requirements and compatibility

  • A supported GPU driver (AMD, Intel, or NVIDIA) for hardware-accelerated encoding

Frequently asked questions

How do I install gpu-screen-recorder on Omarchy?

Open a terminal and run omarchy pkg add gpu-screen-recorder. The download is 211.4 KB and it takes 452.5 KB once installed. Omarchy pulls in any dependencies automatically.

Is gpu-screen-recorder free?

Free and open source. The package is licensed GPL-3.0-only.

How do I uninstall gpu-screen-recorder?

Run omarchy pkg drop gpu-screen-recorder. It removes the package from your system.

What does gpu-screen-recorder depend on?

The package declares 15 dependencies: ffmpeg, libglvnd, libxcomposite, libxrandr, libxfixes, libxdamage, libx11, libpulse, libva, libdrm, libcap, wayland and more. Omarchy installs them for you.

Is gpu-screen-recorder a desktop app?

No. gpu-screen-recorder has no window of its own; it is a command-line tool, library or system component.

Is gpu-screen-recorder in the official Omarchy repo?

Yes. It is published as gpu-screen-recorder (version 5.12.3-2) in the official Omarchy package repository. dec05eba makes it. Project site: https://git.dec05eba.com/gpu-screen-recorder. This site is unofficial and not affiliated with Omarchy or Omacom.
